checks.Title: Re-enter through change, not summary
checks.Evidence: The opening does show changed present-state details well (Reza's eleven days on floor 43, the corporate promotion, the overlay/Air Tax hierarchy), but several key relational shifts are delivered via direct backstory statements rather than dramatized change — e.g. 'He had not thought about Tavi in a long time — not since the eigenlift terminal by the Bloom Quarter, the morning the split had gone from a feeling to a fact' and 'He'd worked alone for fourteen months,' which summarize the rupture instead of letting the present scene imply it.
checks.Fix: Replace the explicit narration of the Reza/Tavi split and the fourteen-months-alone line with a concrete present-tense detail (a habit, a gesture, an object) that lets readers infer the history without being told it directly.

checks.Title: Reintroduce names like an old friend would
checks.Evidence: Reza and Tavi (Rampart/Cutout) get strong reactivating detail through action and stance ('He wasn't thinking about the door,' Tavi reading the doorway stance 'in a basement in Pilsen'), but returning names dropped in via dossier-like exposition rather than in-voice tags — e.g. Onwe is introduced with zero physical or behavioral tag at all ('Onwe found him at 0800, already three moves into a conversation'), and Vane is introduced mostly through habit-description ('Auda Vane avoided meeting in person when she could') which reads more like backstory than a reactivating gesture.
checks.Fix: Give Onwe and Vane the same treatment as Tavi/Reza — one concrete physical or behavioral beat on first appearance (a gesture, a stance, a tic) rather than a summarized habit or unmarked entrance.

checks.Title: Refresh proprietary terms on a lighter touch than the gateway
Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Multiple acronyms appear without any in-voice expansion before their bare use: 'UBC' is mentioned as 'Universal Basic Credit' but only parenthetically after the term already reads like an aside rather than a clean gloss ('drinking coffee that cost more than his monthly UBC — the Universal Basic Credit that used to be the whole of his money'), which inverts the required order (acronym first, then gloss), and 'NSB'-style terms like 'Φ' (used repeatedly as a bare symbol/unit with no expansion anywhere) and 'Tier 1 rig' are never expanded at all.
checks.Fix: Reorder each instance so the full term appears first in-voice (e.g., 'his monthly Universal Basic Credit, the UBC that used to be the whole of his money') and add an in-voice expansion for Φ and any other unexplained abbreviation at its first appearance.

checks.Title: Pay the previous book its due, then move
checks.Evidence: The prose never names or gestures at what the previous book's ending actually was; it opens cold into a new job (forty-third floor routine, Onwe's orders) and only builds new backstory (Tavi/Reza's split, Pilsen, Vane) without ever confirming a prior victory or cost the returning reader carried away from book one.
checks.Fix: Add an early beat — a line of Reza's or Tavi's internal reflection — that explicitly names and confirms the outcome of the previous book's climax (what was won or lost) before pivoting into the new Spire job.

checks.Title: Open the door the last ending left ajar
checks.Evidence: The prose leans hard on continuity (Reza/Tavi's Pilsen history, the click-signal, the coffee-counter ritual, the split at the eigenlift terminal) but never names a single overarching thread the previous book left ajar the way the rule demands—there's no explicit 'this is the question you left with' moment for a returning reader to latch onto early; instead the backstory arrives piecemeal and inferentially (Tavi's mention that 'he had not thought about Tavi in a long time' and the eigenlift reference come mid-scene, buried in action beats rather than framed as the inherited pull).
checks.Fix: Open with an explicit, early beat that names the specific unresolved question from book one (e.g., why Rampart and Cutout split, or what unfinished business the city itself represents for them) before burying it under new plot, so returning readers immediately recognize the door being reopened and see it complicate rather than just recur.

checks.Title: Reward the long memory without taxing the short one
checks.Evidence: The prose leans heavily on unexplained legacy weight — 'He knew one man who called that working from the inside out,' the click-signal from 'a stairwell in Pilsen,' Reza's unwillingness to even think Tavi's name, and the Rampart/Cutout backstory referenced via the in-world show 'Lacuna' — all of which clearly reward a returning reader but are dense enough (three overlapping mysteries: Pilsen, the split at the eigenlift terminal, the four-years-gone history) that a first-timer may struggle to track who these men are to each other and why the corridor fight matters emotionally, since it's delivered through allusion rather than grounding exposition.
checks.Fix: Add one or two concrete lines early in the Reza/Tavi corridor confrontation that plainly state their shared history (partners, betrayal, the split) in-scene rather than relying entirely on oblique callbacks like the click-signal and unspoken name, so newcomers get the emotional stakes without needing prior-book memory.

checks.Title: Escalate, don't repeat
checks.Evidence: The dual-contract trap ('extract' vs 'terminate' on the same target, held by two people who share Pilsen history) and the corridor fight structurally escalate past a simple heist by forcing former partners into a duel neither wants and resolving it through mutual restraint rather than victory—a beat the first story's frame couldn't have earned without that history. The ending also refuses catharsis: Reza loses his position, Tavi abandons his weapon, and the final image (a new augmented kid signing a slip, mirroring Tavi's own origin) explicitly signals the cycle continuing rather than resetting to a clean win.
